## R Markdown
##Load the Libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(naniar)
library(ggmap)
library(leaflet)
library(sf)
```
##Load in Data
```{r}
insects_ag <- read_csv("data/insects_main.csv") %>% clean_names()
```
#check data structure
```{r}
glimpse(insects_ag)
```
#check NA's
```{r}
insects_ag%>%
  miss_var_summary()
```
#omit the NA's, and assign new name
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na<- insects_ag%>%
na.omit()
```
#yay no more NA's :)
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na%>%
  miss_var_summary()
```
# map
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na %>% 
  select(lat, long) %>% 
  summary()
```

```{r}
register_stadiamaps("824e1e2a-26b0-4511-874e-b93a502f5dce", write = FALSE)
```

```{r}
lat<- c(46.12, 48.75 )
long<- c(10.59, 13.41)
bbox<- make_bbox(long, lat, f=0.05)
```
#map of where the data came from (hopefully)
```{r}
map1<- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom = 5)

ggmap(map1)
```
```{r}
ggmap(map1)+
  geom_point(data=insects_ag_no_na, aes(long, lat), size=0.8)+
  labs(x="longitude", y="latitude", title="sites of data collection")
```
#different color??
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na%>%
  group_by(avg_temp,avg_humidity)%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = avg_temp, fill = avg_humidity))+
  geom_density(color = 'black',
               fill = 'pink3', 
               alpha = 0.3,
               na.rm=TRUE)+
  labs(x = "average temperature",
        title = "average temperature compared to average humidity")
```
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na%>%
  group_by(biomass,landscape_type)%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = biomass, fill = landscape_type))+
  geom_boxplot(na.rm=TRUE)+
  labs(x = "average temperature",
       y = "biomass",
        title = "biomass per landscape type")
```
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na%>%
  group_by(lt_mean_annual_precip,lt_mean_annual_avg_ns_temp)%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lt_mean_annual_avg_ns_temp, y = lt_mean_annual_precip))+
  geom_point(na.rm=TRUE)+
  labs(x = "average temperature",
        title = "uhhhhh")
```



#move this code chunk somewhere else
```{r}
insects_ag_no_na %>%
  group_by(landscape_type) %>%
  select(biomass, landscape_type)%>%
  summarize(mean(biomass))

#Agricultural landscape type has the highest biomass on average
```
